messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE players (
    player_id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name TEXT,
    last_name TEXT,
    hand TEXT,
    birth_date DATE,
    country_code TEXT,
    UNIQUE (player_id)
);

CREATE TABLE matches (
    best_of INT,
    draw_size INT,
    loser_age FLOAT,
    loser_entry TEXT,
    loser_hand TEXT,
    loser_ht INT,
    loser_id INT,
    loser_ioc TEXT,
    loser_name TEXT,
    loser_rank INT,
    loser_rank_points INT,
    loser_seed INT,
    match_num INT,
    minutes INT,
    round TEXT,
    score TEXT,
    surface TEXT,
    tourney_date DATE,
    tourney_id TEXT,
    tourney_level TEXT,
    tourney_name TEXT,
    winner_age FLOAT,
    winner_entry TEXT,
    winner_hand TEXT,
    winner_ht INT,
    winner_id INT,
    winner_ioc TEXT,
    winner_name TEXT,
    winner_rank INT,
    winner_rank_points INT,
    winner_seed INT,
    year INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (winner_id) REFERENCES players(player_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (loser_id) REFERENCES players(player_id)
);

CREATE TABLE rankings (
    ranking_date DATE,
    ranking INT,
    player_id INT,
    ranking_points INT,
    tours INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (player_id) REFERENCES players(player_id)
);

```sql
SELECT
  tourney_date,
  tourney_name,
  round,
  winner_name,
  loser_name,
  minutes,
  score,
  surface,
  tourney_level,
  tourney_id,
  match_num
FROM matches
WHERE minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
one of the names should be the player who won the match

```sql
SELECT
  winner_name AS winning_player,
  loser_name  AS losing_player,
  minutes,
  tourney_date,
  tourney_name,
  round,
  score,
  surface
FROM matches
WHERE minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
also need to get the losing player involved in the match

```sql
SELECT
  winner_name AS winning_player,
  loser_name  AS losing_player,
  minutes,
  tourney_date,
  tourney_name,
  round,
  score,
  surface
FROM matches
WHERE minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
You should also look at the players who were part of this match.

```sql
SELECT
  m.minutes,
  m.tourney_date,
  m.tourney_name,
  m.round,
  m.score,
  m.surface,
  pw.player_id AS winner_id,
  pw.first_name AS winner_first_name,
  pw.last_name  AS winner_last_name,
  pw.country_code AS winner_country,
  pl.player_id AS loser_id,
  pl.first_name AS loser_first_name,
  pl.last_name  AS loser_last_name,
  pl.country_code AS loser_country
FROM matches m
JOIN players pw ON pw.player_id = m.winner_id
JOIN players pl ON pl.player_id = m.loser_id
WHERE m.minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY m.minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
We should also check out the names of the individuals involved in this match.

```sql
SELECT
  m.minutes,
  m.tourney_date,
  m.tourney_name,
  m.round,
  m.score,
  CONCAT(pw.first_name, ' ', pw.last_name) AS winner_full_name,
  CONCAT(pl.first_name, ' ', pl.last_name) AS loser_full_name
FROM matches m
JOIN players pw ON pw.player_id = m.winner_id
JOIN players pl ON pl.player_id = m.loser_id
WHERE m.minutes IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY m.minutes DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
